subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should #91602 be split so broad follow-up enforcement stays under #58450 while the exec/pkill abort gets its own reproducible process-supervisor task?
rationale: The report mixes a product-policy invariant for final replies with a lower-level process-control failure; automation should not conflate those boundaries without maintainer intent.

options.title: Split Exec Repro
options.body: Track the Telegram follow-up invariant under #58450 and create or keep a focused task for reproducing and fixing the exec/pkill abort.

options.title: Keep Combined
options.body: Use #91602 as the combined tracker and require one proof package that covers both Telegram follow-up behavior and process kill semantics.

options.title: Close After Disproof
options.body: Close only if a live current-main Telegram/gateway run disproves both the follow-up loop and the exec abort reports.

recommendation.title: Split Exec Repro
recommendation.body: Track the Telegram follow-up invariant under #58450 and create or keep a focused task for reproducing and fixing the exec/pkill abort.

likelyOwner.reason: The recommended decision starts with the follow-up/commitment policy boundary, where this owner has the clearest related feature history.
